title: Relation Between Angular and Linear Velocity and Acceleration
topicTitle: Relation between angular and linear velocity and acceleration
notes: **Linear to angular:** $\omega = v/r$. A point at the rim of a wheel moves faster in linear speed but has the same angular velocity as a point near the centre.
**Angular to linear:** $v = r\omega$. If $\omega$ is constant, linear speed increases with radius â€” which is why the outer edge of a spinning disc has higher speed.
**Tangential acceleration:** $a_t = r\alpha$. This is the acceleration tangent to the circle, changing the speed along the path.
**Centripetal acceleration:** $a_c = v^2/r = r\omega^2$. This is the inward acceleration required to keep the object moving in a circle.
**Total acceleration:** when both speed and direction change, $\vec{a} = \vec{a}_t + \vec{a}_c$. The two components are perpendicular.
